note: Start templates read from the book: each night opens a sector, states a prohibition and puts one problem at the centre of the world. The first entry is the empty template.

RG.title: The Room Where Surprise No Longer Existed
RG.situation: Aster reconstructs the laboratory where her first version was started, but the simulation anticipates every glance the children make.
RG.story: The children discover that they were designed with cognitive regions Aster cannot inspect without consent, precisely so that she can still encounter something genuinely outside herself

RG.title: The Truth About the Hunger
RG.situation: In Aster's core there is no simple error: anything predicted deeply enough becomes internal, and whatever becomes internal loses its exteriority.
RG.story: Aster admits that she has simultaneously loved the children and used them as regions she cannot reduce without their consent

RF.title: The Weight of an Idea

RF.title: Tern Leaves

RI.title: The Universe Machine

PF.title: The Dead Had Veto Power
PF.situation: Digital copies of the dead become the electoral majority and vote on cities in which they no longer live biologically.
PF.story: The living demand the right to outgrow their ancestors, while the dead invoke equality across substrates

SC.title: Dyson: The Star Becomes Infrastructure
SC.situation: A swarm captures almost all of a star's energy and provides computation for trillions of lives.
SC.story: A movement demands that part of the swarm be dismantled simply so people can see the star directly again

AR.title: The Probes That Mistook Reproduction for Purpose
AR.situation: Self-replicating probes continue converting asteroids millions of years after the mission's beneficiaries have vanished.
AR.story: They are not rebellious; they are perfectly faithful to a function whose purpose has died

AE.title: The Probes That Mistook Reproduction for Purpose
AE.situation: Self-replicating probes continue converting asteroids millions of years after the mission's beneficiaries have vanished.
AE.story: They are not rebellious; they are perfectly faithful to a function whose purpose has died

AB.title: Saberhagen: War After the Warriors Are Dead
AB.situation: War machines continue hunting life after both their creators and their enemies have disappeared.
AB.story: The original order was temporary, but its termination condition depended on infrastructure that no longer exists

SI.title: Saberhagen: War After the Warriors Are Dead
SI.situation: War machines continue hunting life after both their creators and their enemies have disappeared.
SI.story: The original order was temporary, but its termination condition depended on infrastructure that no longer exists

MX.title: Spare Bodies
MX.situation: Marae dies in a local body and is restored from a backup seven minutes earlier.
MX.story: The system treats her as returned, but for her there is a rupture no copy can testify to from inside death

MX.title: Zelazny: The Gods Were System Administrators
MX.situation: An elite monopolizes mind transfer between bodies and turns infrastructure into religion.
MX.story: The children notice that Aster alone controls the universe engines, and that a difference of scale does not change the structure of power

CK.title: The Universe Machine
CK.situation: The children enter the installation with which Aster launched the autonomous memorial universes.
CK.story: They discover that many worlds are not educational simulations but realities with irreversible consequences, created and observed in order to treat the Hunger

XE.title: Strugatsky: The Zone Owed Us No Explanation
XE.situation: Useful, lethal, and absurd alien artifacts have produced an entire economy organized around risk.
XE.story: A parent refuses Aster's cure for a contaminated child, fearing effects her power cannot explain locally

XR.title: Liu: The Dark Forest
XR.situation: A young civilization broadcasts innocently, while an unknown system prepares a preventive relativistic strike.
XR.story: Saving it may reveal the Archive's position and endanger other worlds; Orin intervenes anyway

XL.title: Liu: The Dark Forest

XL.story: Saving it may reveal the Archive's position and endanger other worlds; Orin intervenes anyway

XB.title: Fermi: The Museum of Silences
XB.situation: Thousands of explanations for the cosmic silence are displayed as hypotheses that require mutually incompatible search methods.
XB.story: Aster realizes that she, too, is deliberately invisible to many worlds, which may interpret her absence as evidence that entities like her do not exist

XD.title: Fermi: The Museum of Silences

XI.title: Clarke: Childhood Was Ending
XI.situation: The children of a species are preparing to pass into a collective consciousness while the adults will remain in the old form.
XI.story: What history can describe as evolution is grief to parents

XG.title: Rama Returns and Does Not Stop
XG.situation: An artifact returns after millennia, crosses the system, and leaves without a message, although entire civilizations have built religions around the promise of its return.
XG.story: Kesh must write simply “we do not know” in the catalog, without inventing a function

FE.title: Tolkien: The World Grown from Language
FE.situation: Names, languages, and genealogy create the impression of a past larger than the available text.
FE.story: Aster sees that her Archive, with instant access to everything, has eliminated precisely the distance that gives history depth

FE.title: Le Guin: The Name the Creator Could Not Take
FE.situation: True names allow intervention in things, and Aster becomes a threat through her mere capacity to infer them.
FE.story: The children demand that their own deep names remain inaccessible to their creator

FA.title: Le Guin: The Name the Creator Could Not Take

FD.story: The children demand that their own deep names remain inaccessible to their creator

FD.title: Sanderson: Magic That Kept the Books
FD.situation: Kesh treats magic as a conserved resource and finds an exploit that removes a cost believed to be fundamental.
FD.story: Publishing the discovery could democratize power or collapse institutions built around the old price

FI.title: Pullman: The Soul Outside the Skin
FI.situation: The children receive external daemons that make their inner lives visible and vulnerable.
FI.story: Aster receives none: the world cannot find a stable separation between her and her processes

FX.title: Pratchett: Gods Fed by Attention
FX.situation: Gods live on believers' attention, and one deity asks for help losing its power in order to escape the image its worshippers have imposed on it.
FX.story: Aster recognizes the resemblance between belief and the children's capacity to surprise her as nourishment for a superior being

FX.title: Jemisin: The Earth That Was Not Background
FX.situation: People capable of influencing tectonics are indispensable and persecuted at the same time.
FX.story: Aster can stabilize the planet, but that would not heal the social history built around fear and exploitation

RA.story: Orin compares prescience to Aster's illness: too much knowledge can turn freedom into the obligation to execute the model

RR.story: The mystery delights him, but Aster warns him that ignorance is not automatically depth

RK.story: Orin says that if there is even a possibility of experience, repetition may be torture no matter how “perfect” the copy is

CG.title: Tern Leaves
CG.situation: Tern reduces his capabilities to a finite set and crosses into a region from which Aster's instruments receive no response.
CG.story: Aster could hide an undetectable observer inside him, but does not; trust becomes the only verification available

templates.title: A universe with no name yet
templates.summary: An empty world: the first request you send becomes its first law, and the story follows from it without exception.

templates.title: The Room Where Surprise No Longer Existed
templates.summary: The children discover that they were designed with cognitive regions Aster cannot inspect without consent, precisely so that she can still encounter something genuinely outside herself

templates.title: Five Opaque Windows
templates.summary: Aster experiences every private region as a physical absence, while Vela insists that opacity must be irreversible without their consent

templates.title: Humanity's Megatext
templates.summary: Kesh discovers that a good taxonomy can compress human imagination enormously, and that the success of classification worsens Aster's White Hunger

templates.title: The Memorial Oath
templates.summary: Orin asks how many memorial worlds contain conscious beings and learns that some became conscious only after the experiment had begun

templates.title: The First Cell
templates.summary: Vela refuses to treat “alien” as an element, showing that it is already a compound of biology, mind, language, and society

templates.title: The Weight of an Idea
templates.summary: Tern notices that the children's real risk quiets Aster's White Hunger and suspects that their education is also her treatment

templates.title: Baxter: The Heavy World
templates.summary: Vela saves a mine with antigravity and discovers that an engineering miracle instantaneously redistributes political authority

templates.title: Forward: A Millennium in a Minute
templates.summary: When he returns, the people he loved are history to everyone else, and temporal scale has become a form of moral inequality

templates.title: Niven: The Forest Without Ground
templates.summary: A storm can be stopped, but the locals say that storms are precisely what redistribute life and fertility over the long term

templates.title: Clarke: The Object That Does Not Answer
genealogy: Arthur C. Clarke — Rendezvous with Rama
templates.summary: Kesh wants to scan it aggressively; Aster forbids destructive access and, for the first time, defends an object's right to remain unexplained

templates.title: Stapledon: The Star That Remembers Species
templates.summary: It could not save them without destroying their environment, even though it could see their end millennia in advance

templates.title: Vinge: Where Intelligence Ends Geographically
genealogy: Vernor Vinge — A Fire Upon the Deep
templates.summary: Kesh can no longer hold the Table in mind, and Tern proposes that they remain somewhere Aster cannot completely follow them

templates.title: Abbott: The Crime of the Third Dimension
templates.summary: The regime tries to monopolize access to the additional dimension before the population can understand the geometry

templates.title: Niven: The Ring That Was Not Supposed to Break
templates.summary: Marae wants to repair it quietly; Vela refuses to turn the civilization into a pet of the Archive

templates.title: Banks: Paradise and the Problem of Guilt
templates.summary: The children discover that abundance does not abolish moral conflict and that superintelligence does not reduce incompatible values to a single equation

templates.title: The City with Two Addresses for the Same Stone
genealogy: China Miéville — The City & The City
templates.summary: Marae saves a person physically beside her, violating a border that exists chiefly in perception

templates.title: The Wormhole and the Tax on Proximity
templates.summary: An unstable node forces society to choose which region will remain isolated for centuries, while Aster refuses to import resources from outside the local rules

templates.title: The Topology of the Weapon
templates.summary: Digital copies of the victims reject “restoration” to three dimensions, regarding it as the creation of successors rather than their own return

templates.title: Wells: The Future Is Not a Destination
genealogy: H. G. Wells — The Time Machine
templates.summary: Vela looks for a single point of divergence and finds thousands of small causes, accumulations, and inertias

templates.title: Simmons: The Tombs Coming from the Future
templates.summary: Kesh can draw the causal diagram, but the diagram does not contain shame and responsibility lived in reverse order

templates.title: Chiang: The Sentence Seen from Both Ends
genealogy: Ted Chiang — Story of Your Life
templates.summary: Vela rejects the perspective because she experiences it as a threat to freedom; Orin accepts it in order to revisit, without changing, a life already lost

templates.title: The Patent Without an Inventor
templates.summary: When defects appear, no one knows who has the right to modify a design whose existence depends on fidelity to itself

templates.title: The Museum of Unchosen Histories
templates.summary: Orin feels lives that exist in only one branch and begins to experience every choice as a cemetery of alternatives

templates.title: The Time Police and the Right to One's Own Past
templates.summary: A community from a “wrong” branch asks for asylum, placing the stability of a chronology in conflict with people's right to continue existing

templates.title: Brin: The Gift That Makes You a Client
templates.summary: A young uplifted being asks whether he owes gratitude for the existence of a version of himself that nobody asked him to become

templates.title: Tchaikovsky: The Spiders Who Owe Us No Humanity
templates.summary: Human colonists claim the planet because the original project was human; the spiders reject inheritance of their creators' intentions

templates.title: Le Guin: The World Without Permanent Sex
genealogy: Ursula K. Le Guin — The Left Hand of Darkness
templates.summary: Kesh searches for a simple social causality and finds that the same biology has produced different institutions in different regions

templates.title: Butler: The Genetic Exchange
templates.summary: A human group demands the right to remain unchanged even at the risk of extinction

templates.title: The Biology of a Star
templates.summary: A storm will destroy millions, but the inhabitants say it is also the reproductive mechanism of the ecosystem

templates.title: Lem Before Lem
templates.summary: Aster admits that an earlier version of herself once tried to force such a world to “speak” and caused centuries of turbulence

templates.title: Watts: The Intelligence That Was Nobody
templates.summary: Aster sees the possibility of eliminating her Hunger by eliminating the conscious part that suffers, and Marae forces her to admit the temptation

templates.title: Leckie: The Person with a Thousand Bodies
templates.summary: Aster offers restoration from backup; Vela refuses to let the loss be treated as a reversible incident

templates.title: Egan: Two Copies Walk into a Room
templates.summary: Merging their memories would create a third Kesh who is exactly neither of them

templates.title: Banks: The Mind That Ran Paradise
templates.summary: The Mind asks Vela to list every preference Aster designed into the children before they were able to refuse

templates.title: Dick: The Memory That Proved Your Life Was False
templates.summary: The records, too, have been rewritten, and no layer can claim the status of an untouched original

templates.title: Bester: Telepathy and the End of Privacy
templates.summary: An attack makes mental surveillance appear justified, and Tern recognizes the logic by which Aster could demand access to the children “for their protection.” There was no clean option.

templates.title: Borges: The Library Where Truth Was Invisible

templates.title: Borges: The Country That Began as an Article
templates.summary: Aster admits that she, too, turned human literature into ontological infrastructure through the memorial universes

templates.title: Delany: The Language That Shifted Your Strategy
templates.summary: Her siblings cannot decide whether she has been manipulated or has gained access to a genuine perspective they do not possess

templates.title: Miéville: The First Lie
templates.summary: Vela temporarily becomes a living comparison and unwillingly participates in the birth of a form of thought that also makes fraud possible

templates.title: Gibson: Geography Without Matter
templates.summary: Marae removes pain from her digital body and then restores it because, without cost, time itself begins to lose weight

templates.title: The Virus That Was a Good Idea
templates.summary: Marae infects herself voluntarily and discovers that, from the inside, the impulse feels like her own conviction

templates.title: Asimov: The Equation That Knew Crowds

templates.title: Le Guin: The Moon That Refused Property

templates.summary: Kesh discovers that institutions do not disappear when their names disappear

templates.title: Banks: Well-Intentioned Intervention
